key_insight: SANA-Video 2.0 shows that high-quality video generation can be made much more efficient by combining linear attention with occasional softmax attention anchors. This hybrid design keeps the long-sequence scaling benefits of linear attention while matching the quality of full-softmax video diffusion transformers.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high compute and memory cost of generating long, high-resolution videos with standard full-softmax attention, which limits scaling and makes single-GPU 720p video generation difficult.
method: Introduces a unified hybrid video diffusion transformer at 5B and 14B scales.
Uses Hybrid Linear-Softmax Attention: gated linear attention for O(N)-dominated mixing and periodic gated-softmax anchors to preserve global consistency.
Designed to generate high-quality video up to 720p efficiently on a single GPU.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a practical path to stronger video generation without the usual quadratic attention cost. It can reduce hardware requirements while preserving quality, making large-scale video diffusion more deployable and scalable.

paper_title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
paper_authors: Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Yitong Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu
